document_check.note: Wang J, Liang X, Lu J, Zhang W, Chen Q, Li X, Chen J, Zhang X, Zhang B. Cortical and subcortical gray matter abnormalities in mild cognitive impairment. Neuroscience 557 (2024) 81-88. 24 MCI versus 22 normal controls from one hospital. Matches Wang et al. 2024a.

cited_result: Reduced bilateral hippocampal volume in MCI compared with normal controls (left p = 0.006, right p = 0.008, FDR-corrected, adjusted for age, sex, education and TIV), from the voxel-based volumetry analysis in a single-centre sample of 24 MCI and 22 NC.
tool_reason: The cited result is a group difference in a structural measure (hippocampal volume) between MCI and controls measured at one time point, not a model or accuracy estimate. Item mapping used: exposure = cognitive group assignment, condition = MCI diagnostic criteria, outcome = hippocampal volume.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: Handedness, education minimum, exclusions and group-specific inclusion thresholds are stated.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: All participants were right-handed and had received a minimum of 9 years of education. Individuals who had a history of stroke, other neuropsychiatric disorders (Parkinson’s disease, brain tumor, epilepsy, etc.), severe depression or anxiety, and MRI contraindications were excluded.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The recruitment site and demographic and cognitive characteristics by group (Table 1) are reported. Recruitment period and method are not stated.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: All participants were recruited from neurology clinic of Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (cognitive group assignment) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: A standard battery (MMSE, MoCA, PVLT, TMT, BNT, VFT) was administered by an experienced neuropsychologist to all participants.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: The cognitive assessments for all subjects were performed by an experienced neuropsychologist.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: The MCI criteria are stated, but no published diagnostic framework is cited. 'Objective evidence of memory impairment' is not operationalised (no test or cut-off), and the stated MMSE range for MCI (25 to 26) conflicts with the reported MCI MMSE of 28.0 plus or minus 1.4. The control criteria allow CDR 0.5, and the authors concede that MCI identification rested mainly on rating scales.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: MCI subjects: had a memory complaint and objective evidence of memory impairment; Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores between 25 and 26, Montreal cognitive assessment scale (MoCA) scores between 19 and 25; Hachinski scores less than or equal to 4
signalling.page: 2 (journal p. 82); Table 1 on page 3 reports MMSE 28.0 ± 1.4 in MCI

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education and head size were identified as covariates; the groups differed in age.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: There were no significant differences in sex distribution and education level, but the two groups differed in terms of age (p = 0.038).

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: The volumetric group comparison is adjusted by GLM covariates.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: A general linear model with a two-sample t-test design was employed to investigate group differences in subcortical structure volume controlling for age, sex, years of education and TIV.

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcome (hippocampal volume) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: A single 3 T scanner and automated segmentation (SPM12 DARTEL preprocessing, FSL-FIRST) were applied identically to all participants. Segmentation quality control is not reported.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All imaging data were acquired on a 3 T Philips Achieva TX MRI scanner using an 8-channel head coil in Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. ... the FSL-FIRST (https://fsl.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl/fslwiki/FIRST), a Bayesian model-based segmentation tool, was employed to segment subcortical nuclei

domains.rationale: Covariate-adjusted GLM across 14 structures with FDR correction. The hippocampal results survive correction.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: The false discovery rate (FDR) correction was used to measure potentially significant between-group differences.

applicability.rationale: Clinic-recruited MCI and controls, relevant to the review's MCI-versus-control structural question. It is a single centre and MCI subtypes are not separated.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 1 to 3 and 5 to 8 Yes; item 4 Unclear)
overall_rationale: The critical items (confounder identification, confounder strategy, valid outcome measurement, appropriate analysis) are all Yes, so under the review's rule the result is not high risk. It is not low because the MCI case definition is not a cited standard and is internally inconsistent with the reported MMSE values. The small sample (46) and the unreported recruitment method also limit precision and representativeness.
appraiser: model reader (primary), under the operator's delegation of 2026-09-28
